quests.title: Word from Bael Modan
quests.description:
Wrangler Tull. Come round the fire, you're in the smoke.

The dwarves have been digging at Bael Modan for years and nobody here has minded very much.

I want to be fair about that. Digging is digging. They turned up, they put a hole in some ground nobody was grazing, and for a long while that was the whole story and the camp had bigger ones.

Word now is they've built a proper fortress over it. Bael'dun Keep.

That's a different sentence.

You don't build a keep over a hole unless you intend to be at the bottom of that hole for a very long time, or unless you expect somebody to come and stop you.

Either way it stops being mining.

Go and see for yourself before Camp Taurajo commits any real attention south.

I'd rather look foolish for asking than find out from a dwarf.

objectives.label: Bael'dun Keep, above the dig at Bael Modan

quests.accept_text: Bael Modan, south - look for the keep over the dig.
quests.turn_in_text:
A whole keep. Just for digging up old bones and ore.

Dwarves.

Still - good to know what we're dealing with, and better to know it now.

quests.title: The Dwarven Excavation
quests.description:
Keep's confirmed, so now the dig itself.

And I'd like to put a number on the thing that's actually bothering me, because it isn't the hole.

That excavation has expanded further into tauren-claimed ground every season I've watched it. Not once. Every season.

A little each time. Never enough to be worth a complaint, and that's precisely the method - whether or not anyone down there is thinking of it as one.

I drove kodo past that boundary stone for twenty years. It is now a long way inside their workings and nobody ever crossed a line, because the line moved under it a yard at a time.

So I want the crews thinned.

Miners, engineers, it doesn't matter to me.

Just fewer dwarves expanding that dig, and a season where the stone stays where it is.
quests.accept_text: The excavation crews at the Bael Modan dig.
quests.turn_in_text:
That'll slow their digging a season at least.

I'll go and look at the boundary stone this week. First time in three years I'll be able to stand at it.

Thank you.

quests.title: General Twinbraid's Folly
quests.description:
[Elder Longtread takes his time with this one.]

I have watched General Twinbraid grow bolder with every site he claims.

And I want to be exact about why I'm asking, because this will look like vengeance and it is not.

I have no quarrel with dwarves. I've traded with them. I knew one well, some years back, and I'd have called him a friend if either of us had used the word.

Twinbraid doesn't dig for ore anymore. Not really.

He digs for territory and calls it prospecting, and the calling-it is the part that matters, because a man who's found a word for what he's doing has stopped hearing anyone tell him not to.

He has stopped respecting any boundary at all. Not ours. Not his own Keep's.

Someone needs to remind him where Bael'dun's walls actually end.

I'd have preferred that to be a conversation. It was, twice.
quests.accept_text: At Bael'dun Keep, with the dig crews he commands.
quests.turn_in_text:
Twinbraid's dead, and the digging stops for a while.

It'll start again eventually. It always does - somebody else will have the same idea and a better word for it.

But this bought the land some peace, and peace is bought, never given.

quests.title: Raptor Hides for the Docks
quests.description:
Fishmonger Gribble. Yes, I know what the stall says. Hear me out.

I've got a side trade in raptor hide.

Fish is the business. Fish is reliable, fish is boring, and fish has kept this stall open through two bad years.

Raptor hide is the margin.

And the Sunscale out at the Grounds east of here are the closest real supply on this whole coast - everything else comes up from the south at a price that eats the point of it.

Bring them back whole, as whole as you can manage.

That's not fussiness. A hide with a hole through the middle is worth about a third, because the buyers cut panels and a panel has to be clean. I've watched a man price a perfectly good hide down to nothing over one spear mark.

Whole as you can. I'll make it worth your trip.
quests.accept_text: Sunscale raptors at the Grounds, east of Ratchet.
quests.turn_in_text:
Good hide. Barely torn.

This'll fetch a real price at the docks, and I'll not be telling anyone where it came from.

quests.title: Thinning the Grounds
quests.description:
Dockmaster Brindle. Walk and talk, I've got a tide.

I have had one too many shipments delayed by raptors.

Not attacked. Delayed - and I want the distinction on the record because every time I raise this, somebody asks how many drivers I've lost and the answer is none.

Here's what actually happens. The Sunscale stray too close to the coast road. The drivers see them. The drivers stop, or turn back, or take the long way round, and a shipment that should take two days takes four.

Nobody dies. Everybody's late. And late, in this port, is a contract.

I've lost two this quarter to a problem that has never once drawn blood.

So: thin them back from the Grounds itself.

Not the road - the road's a symptom. They're coming off the Grounds because there's too many on it.

My shipments cannot keep dodging claws.
quests.accept_text: At the Raptor Grounds, back from the coast road.
quests.turn_in_text:
Fewer raptors between here and the Grounds.

The road's clear. For now, which is the only tense this port deals in.

quests.title: The One They Call Brontus
quests.description:
Now this one's half business and I'll tell you which half.

Brontus.

Every sailor who's been inland has a story about that kodo, and I've been collecting them for six years without ever intending to.

Ancient. Elite - and I use that word deliberately, because the stories agree on it and sailors agree on nothing. A beast old enough to have a reputation that arrived in this port before I did.

Half of those stories are probably true. That's my honest estimate and it's a generous one.

The trouble is which half, because the dangerous half is real whichever way round it goes. He roams Blackthorn Ridge and my drivers go round it, and going round costs me.

So: hunt him.

Bring back proof and I'll believe the rest of it.

And then I'll tell the story myself, badly, for years. I want you to know that going in.
quests.turn_in_text:
You actually did it.

I'll be telling this story myself now, and I'll be getting it wrong within a fortnight.

Well earned.

quests.title: Zulraka's Toll
quests.description:
Zulraka. Dockhand - which means I walk, mon, more than anybody here realises.

There's a silithid dig south-east of this port, spiralling down into the earth, and I've heard it's been growing.

Now I know how that sounds coming from a dockhand. I'm not a scholar and I've got no business having a theory about bugs.

Here's my business.

I walk the coast road every week. Same road, same stretch, since I came to this port - and the thing about walking a road for years is you learn what it sounds like under your feet.

It's different past the fourth mile. Hollower. Has been since spring.

If that dig keeps going it undermines the road, and then one week it isn't a road and I'm on it.

Go look. Tell me how deep it goes.

I'd rather know than keep guessing at it every Thursday.

objectives.label: the silithid dig at the Broodspiral

quests.accept_text: The silithid dig south-east of Ratchet.
quests.turn_in_text:
Deeper than I hoped. Not as deep as I feared.

Thank you for checking, mon. I'll sleep easier walking that road - and I'll still walk the inland side of it.

quests.title: The Quilboar Territories
quests.description:
Krunk Anvilfist. Mind the anvil, it's hot and it's been hot since Tuesday.

Blackthorn Ridge, north of Razorfen Kraul.

Razormane country. And the reports say it's thick with them now - properly held, not just wandered through.

I'd like that confirmed before I waste a warband on a rumour, and I've wasted one before and I've not been allowed to forget it.

Here's what I need and it isn't a headcount.

I need to know whether that ridge is a camp or a position. A camp is quilboar living somewhere. A position is quilboar holding something, and the two look identical from a distance and are completely different problems.

So go up and survey it.

And if there's a name up there - somebody they follow - I want that most of all. Numbers I can plan around. A name changes what I send.

objectives.label: Blackthorn Ridge, north of Razorfen Kraul

quests.accept_text: Blackthorn Ridge, north of Razorfen Kraul.
quests.turn_in_text:
Confirmed, then. Thick with quilboar, and at least one real threat worth naming.

I'll pass this up the chain. And this time they'll read it, because it's got a name in it.

quests.title: Razormane Incursion
quests.description:
Ridge confirmed, so we bleed it.

And I'll be straight about the goal, which is not conquest and never was.

I want the Razormane to reconsider testing us.

That's it. I'm not taking that ridge - I haven't the men and I wouldn't hold it if I had. What I want is for the next quilboar who suggests pushing toward the southern trade routes to be argued with by somebody in his own camp.

That argument only happens if this raid costs them.

A small raid they shrug off. A real one gets talked about round their own fire, and the talking is the whole objective.

The stalkers work the ridge, so that's where you'll find them.

Whichever rank you come across. It's not about which ones - it's about how many, and how obviously.
quests.accept_text: The Razormane stalkers on Blackthorn Ridge.
quests.turn_in_text:
The ridge won't forget this raid.

And they'll think twice next time, which is a thing I can't make happen with a warband and you just did in an afternoon.

quests.title: Hagg Taurenbane
quests.description:
There's a champion up on that ridge and I need him dead before he becomes a story.

Hagg Taurenbane.

He's earned the name the hard way - ask any patrol that's crossed him and lived, and there are fewer of those than I'd like to say out loud.

Here's the part that's actually urgent, and it isn't the killing.

Solo warbands have stopped patrolling that stretch. Entirely. Not after an order - they just stopped, one at a time, and nobody reported it and I only noticed from the duty rosters.

That's what a reputation does before the fighting even starts. He's taken a mile of ground off us without leaving his ridge.

Kill him before the Razormane rally round the idea of him.

Because once a tribe decides a man is unkillable, killing him stops being enough - you have to do it in front of them, and that's a much harder afternoon.
quests.accept_text: On Blackthorn Ridge, among the Razormane.
quests.turn_in_text:
He bled like anything else does.

The stories will outlive him anyway - they always do.

At least they're just stories now, and the patrols will go back out.

quests.title: Snizzle's Silithid Curiosity
quests.description:
Snizzle Boltcrank. Don't touch anything on that bench, most of it is mid-experiment and one of it is mid-argument.

There's a genuinely new silithid tunnel network south-east of Ratchet.

New. I want to dwell on that word because everybody skips past it.

Silithid nests are old. That's the whole character of the things - you find one, and it turns out it's been there since before anybody local had a word for it. I have never in my career heard of one appearing.

This one appeared.

So something changed, recently, in a species that does not change, and I would very much like to know what.

I want chitin. Hardened chitin - the kind that comes off something that has actually fought for its life, not the soft rubbish off surface vermin.

The hardening is the data. A creature that's had to armour itself was expecting something.
quests.accept_text: Off the silithid in the new tunnels south-east of Ratchet.
quests.turn_in_text:
Fascinating structure. Look at the layering - that's not growth, that's response.

This'll keep me occupied for weeks.

Thank you. Genuinely, and I don't say that at this bench.

quests.title: Into the Broodspiral
quests.description:
Apothecary Zurm. Come in, mind the step, ignore the smell - it's the work, not the room.

I have become concerned about what's at the centre of that tunnel network, and I'd like to explain the shape of the concern.

It isn't the silithid. Silithid are a known quantity and an unpleasant one and we have dealt with nests before.

It's the spiral.

A nest spreads. It goes where the digging is easy, it branches, it wanders - that's what every silithid warren I've studied does and it's what makes them survivable.

This one descends in a spiral, which is to say it is going somewhere specific, and something decided where.

So I want it confirmed properly rather than rumoured about by dockhands.

Clear the guardians off the outer tunnels.

And then we'll know whether this is worth Orgrimmar's real attention, which is a sentence I have been avoiding writing for a month.
quests.accept_text: The outer tunnels of the Broodspiral, south-east of Ratchet.
quests.turn_in_text:
Ten down, and the tunnels keep going deeper than that.

Whatever's at the centre of that spiral, it's not finished growing.

I've written that down and I dislike it in my own handwriting.

quests.title: The Broodkeeper
quests.description:
Outer tunnels are confirmed dangerous, which I'd expected, and confirmed organised, which I had not.

There's a Broodkeeper deeper in the spiral. A caster of sorts, tending the egg chambers.

Tending. That's the word I keep coming back to and it's the reason I'm sending you rather than writing another report.

Silithid don't tend. They lay and they leave and the hive works or it doesn't. Every text I own agrees on that and two of them are from people who died establishing it.

Something down there is looking after eggs deliberately, and the growth rate we've measured is exactly what you'd expect if it were.

Every day it lives, the hive gets bigger. Not linearly.

Kill it and buy the surface world some real time - which is all I'm claiming, because the eggs are already laid and nothing kills those but years.
quests.accept_text: The egg chambers deeper in the Broodspiral.
quests.turn_in_text:
The egg chambers have gone quiet. For now.

It won't stay that way forever. It'll stay that way long enough, which is the only promise anyone in my trade gets to make.

quests.title: The Queen's Silence
quests.description:
I've confirmed what I feared and I'm going to say it plainly rather than hedge it in the way I've been hedging it for a fortnight.

Something massive rules the centre of that spiral.

A Queen. And everything down there answers to her, which is the part that turns a nest into a problem.

Here's the distinction and it's the whole of my argument.

An unorganised hive is a hazard. It eats what's near it, it grows where the ground allows, and you can live beside one for a generation if you're sensible about which fields you plant.

An organised one decides.

And I have watched this one dig a spiral toward something, tend its own eggs, and armour its workers against a threat it was anticipating - and I do not know what it's anticipating, and that is the single most uncomfortable sentence in my notes.

Kill her and the hive loses its reason to keep growing.

This is the real fight. Everything before it was the approach, including the parts that nearly killed you.
quests.turn_in_text:
The Broodspiral is silent now.

It won't stay empty - nothing in the Barrens ever does, and I'd not insult you by pretending otherwise.

But for now it's quiet. You did something genuinely difficult down there. Don't let anyone tell you otherwise, and somebody will.

quests.title: The Beastcaller's Request
quests.description:
Beastcaller Nira. Quietly, there's one sleeping.

I want Sunscale eggs. From the Grounds east of here, off the lashtails that guard them.

Three, and unbroken if you can manage it, and I'll tell you exactly why that's worth more to me than a wagon of hides.

I think I can hatch one.

Not tame a caught raptor - that's been done and it's a miserable business for everyone involved, and the animal never stops knowing. Hatch one. Have it know me before it knows anything else.

I've been working toward it for six years and I've had two eggs in that time and lost both, one to a crack I didn't see and one to my own impatience.

So: carefully.

Unbroken means unbroken. A hairline is a dead raptor three weeks later and you won't know until it is.

A hatched raptor's worth more to me than a dozen hides. It's worth more to me than most things.
quests.accept_text: Sunscale eggs from the Grounds east of camp. Unbroken.
quests.turn_in_text:
Still warm!

This might actually work. I'm not going to say more than that - I've said more than that before.

Thank you. Truly, this is rare work.

quests.title: Spiritcarver's Balance
quests.description:
Sit with me. I've been needing somebody who's actually seen it rather than heard about it.

Spiritcarver Dennok.

Here's what I've been turning over, and I'd like to lay it out in order because the order is the thing that worries me.

Quilboar against quilboar, north. That's been true for generations and I'd have called it the natural state of the plain.

Dwarves digging where they shouldn't, south. Three years of that, maybe four, and getting faster.

And something ancient waking in the earth beneath both of them.

Any one of those is a season's problem. I've carved totems for worse.

All three at once, in one lifetime, on one plain - that's not three problems. That's one thing happening, and I cannot see the shape of it, and I have been staring at it long enough to know that staring is no longer helping.

So tell me what you saw. All of it, in your own order.

I need to think this through with somebody whose hands were in it.
quests.accept_text: Sit with Spiritcarver Dennok a while.
quests.turn_in_text:
You've given me a clearer picture than I had, and a worse one.

Whatever comes of it, at least I'm not guessing anymore.

Thank you. Come back if you see more - and you will.
